Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp.'s Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are David Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Alex Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; and Maria Lopez, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to David Thompson.

David Thompson: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp. delivered solid results in Q2, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved robust production growth and meaningful capex efficiencies across our key basins. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on exploration successes and key well results that exceeded expectations. We are focused on expanding our future development plans and unlocking substantial resource potential across our portfolio. Finally, we are taking steps to further strengthen our balance sheet through disciplined deleveraging and liquidity management.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.1 billion, up 22% year-over-year. Operating income was $750 million, and net income was $550 million. We generated $650 million in free cash flow and returned $280 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $12.4 billion in total debt and $2.8 billion in cash.

Good morning, everyone. As we dive deeper into our financials, I'd like to provide a detailed walkthrough of our capital expenditure—or Capex—breakdown for the first half of 2024, focusing on the key pillars of Drilling, Completion, and Facilities. Our full-year Capex guidance remains firmly at $2.8 billion, weighted 65% toward the back half to support our accelerated drilling inventory turn in the Permian and emerging Eagle Ford pads. Year-to-date, we've deployed $1.18 billion against a budgeted $1.45 billion, delivering a favorable 19% underrun, or $270 million below plan. This efficiency stems from our relentless focus on operational excellence, supply chain optimizations, and proactive cost management amid a backdrop of moderating service inflation—now running at just 2-3% YoY for most D&C categories, down from 15% peaks in 2022.

Let me break this down category by category, with budget versus actuals, key drivers, and regional insights.

Drilling: Budget $525 million vs. Actual $460 million (12% underrun).

Drilling represents about 37% of our full-year program and has been our strongest performer YTD. We spudded 42 wells against a plan of 48, but achieved this with exceptional well times—averaging 18 days from spud to rig release per Permian horizontal, a 15% improvement over H1 2023. This was driven by our adoption of high-spec Cat 1250 rigs from Nabors, paired with advanced PDC bits from Halliburton that extended run lengths to over 6,000 feet laterally without trips. Drilling costs per foot fell to $450 from a budgeted $520, thanks to 10% deflation in directional drilling services and our in-house mud program, which cut logistics costs by 8% in the Delaware Basin.

Regionally, Permian ops—our core 70% allocation—accounted for $320 million actual spend, under budget by $50 million due to pad drilling efficiencies on our Waha North pads, where we've stacked three rigs continuously. In the Eagle Ford, $90 million deployed beat our IP30 expectations on Blackhawk horizontals, validating our $10 million pilot into extended laterals up to 12,000 feet. Bakken exposure remains minimal at $50 million, focused on high-NGL content Fort Berthold acreage. Looking ahead, we're guiding flat drilling costs into Q3, with rig counts steady at 12 gross (9.2 net), positioning us to exit the year with 180 drilled but uncompleted wells—our DUC inventory—for optimal capital allocation.

Completion: Budget $780 million vs. Actual $825 million (6% overrun).

Completion, at 44% of the program, saw a modest overrun as we leaned into higher-return opportunities. We completed 55 wells versus 50 planned, pumping over 1.2 million stages with an average of 55 stages per well—up 10% from prior year. Intensity remains elite at 3,500 pounds of proppant per foot and 25 barrels per foot of fluid, utilizing slickwater designs optimized via our proprietary frac modeling software in partnership with Liberty Energy.

The overrun was intentional: $45 million incremental spend accelerated completions on six high-GIP Wolfcamp pads in the Midland Basin, where early IP30s are tracking 1,800 Boe/d—20% above type curve. Costs per stage held at $25,000, flat to budget despite 5% wireline inflation, offset by bulk sand purchasing from Hi-Crush at $45/ton FOB mine. Regional split: Permian $580 million (70%), Eagle Ford $180 million (22%) with Pearsall tight oil focus, and $65 million offshore GoM tiebacks via our 25% stake in the Winterfell field subsea development. This front-loading enhances 2024 production guidance to 145-155 MBoepd, a 12% beat to consensus.

Strategically, we're pioneering 'cube' developments with simultaneous fracs across 48 wells on our Stateline leasehold, reducing cycle times by 25% and unlocking 15% NPV uplift per our internal economics at $70 WTI.

Facilities: Budget $145 million vs. Actual $95 million (35% underrun).

Facilities cap the breakdown at 19% of spend, with significant deferrals to preserve liquidity for D&C. Actuals reflect $50 million under plan, primarily from phased rollout of water infrastructure and gas gathering. Key projects include $40 million on our $200 million Permian water recycling facility—now 60% complete, targeting 80% recycle rates by Q4 to slash disposal costs from $1.50/bbl to $0.50/bbl, in line with Pioneer and ExxonMobil's ESG benchmarks.

Regionally, $55 million in Permian midstream tie-ins to Waha headers amid ongoing basis volatility (-$1.50/MMBtu discount), $25 million Eagle Ford compression upgrades for richer gas cuts (45% NGL yield), and $15 million GoM platform retrofits for subsea pumps. The underrun allows flexibility for bolt-ons; we've already allocated $20 million to fast-track electrification on two pads, cutting Scope 1 emissions 30% via solar-plus-battery microgrids from NextEra.

Overall insights and outlook: Net-net, our $270 million YTD underrun—equivalent to 2.5 turns on our 10% IRR threshold—demonstrates capital discipline amid WTI averaging $82 and Henry Hub at $2.70. We've captured $120 million in savings from vendor negotiations (e.g., 12% off Patterson-UTI day rates) and AI-driven drilling analytics, mirroring Continental Resources' playbook. Inventory quality shines: 5+ years of Tier 1 locations at < $40 breakeven, with 70% Permian core.

For H2, expect $1.65 billion deployment, ramping to 20 spuds/month, with Facilities spend normalizing to budget. This cadence supports free cash flow of $800-900 million at strip prices, 45% payout to shareholders via buybacks and base dividend. We're well-positioned in a supply-constrained market, with OPEC+ cuts extending into 2025 tailwinds.

Before handing off, a quick note on our debt profile, which continues to strengthen. As of quarter-end, total gross debt stood at $12.4 billion, down from $14.2 billion at year-end 2023 and $13.8 billion last quarter—a deliberate 13% year-over-year and 10% quarter-over-quarter deleveraging. Breaking it down: Revolving credit facility at $1.2 billion drawn out of $4.5 billion capacity, with $3.3 billion availability; term loans $3.8 billion at blended SOFR-plus-225 bps; unsecured bonds $7.4 billion across five series laddered to 2032, weighted average coupon 4.75%, after refinancing $1.5 billion of higher-coupon notes into cheaper paper, extending maturities to 5.8 years. Fixed-rate debt is now 65% of total.

Net debt, total debt minus $2.8 billion cash, is $9.6 billion—a 32% drop from YE 2023 and $900 million sequentially. Net debt to TTM EBITDAX is 0.9x, down from 1.6x last year, with EBITDAX at $10.7 billion on 15% production growth to 850,000 boe/d and $72/bbl realizations. Gross debt to EBITDAX at 1.2x, debt-to-cap at 28%—below peers. This is fueled by Permian FCF, Bakken surplus, GoM recoveries, and JV-funded Guyana. Cumulative FCF since 2022: $4.2 billion, 50% to debt paydown. 2024 guide: net debt $8-9 billion, sub-0.8x leverage on $4.5-5 billion FCF.

I will now turn the call over to Maria Lopez for an operational update.

Maria Lopez: Thank you, Alex. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 152,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought Waha North pads online, which are expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives.

Good morning, everyone. Before turning it over, I'd like to provide a detailed update on our exploration and drilling activities, which remain the cornerstone of our multi-basin portfolio driving both near-term production growth and long-term value creation. We're focused on high-return, oil-weighted inventory in Tier 1 acreage, leveraging our technical edge in extended laterals, optimized completions, and data-driven sweet spotting. We've deployed $450 million in D&C capex this quarter, in line with our full-year guidance of $1.8 to $2.0 billion, with a rig count averaging 14 across our core assets—up from 12 prior quarter as we accelerate development in response to sustained WTI pricing above $80 per barrel.

Key well results from our flagship Permian Basin operations, where we hold over 60,000 net acres in the Delaware and Midland sub-basins—among the most prolific, comparable to Pioneer Natural Resources' footprint. In Q2, we brought online 28 Delaware wells across Waha North and Monument Draw pads, achieving an average IP30 rate of 1,450 boe/d—14% above type curve and 22% better than prior vintages. Oil cuts averaged 68%, with rich gas supporting $25-30/bbl NGLs amid strong Mont Belvieu spreads.

Powered by Genesis completion design across 85% of Permian program: 4,500-foot laterals pushing to 5,000 feet, 55 stages, 2,200 lbs proppant/ft, proprietary diverters boosting cluster efficiency to 92%. EURs at 1.2 million boe, DDAs down 18% to 22 days via automated systems and Nabors/Helmerich & Payne walking rigs. 99% success rate.

In Eagle Ford, 45,000 net acres in Karnes/DeWitt: spudded 12, turned 10, IP30s 1,800 boe/d (85% liquids), base decline 65% year one, outperforming EOG. Slickwater fracs with CARBO ceramics cut water 12%. De-risked 150 locations, inventory >500 DUCs/undeveloped at sub-$40 breakeven.

Offshore Gulf of Mexico: Lucius South extension in Green Canyon 875 hit 180 ft net pay (+25%), IP 8,000 boe/d, 65-degree API oil with helium-rich gas. Sanctioned two Q1 2025 follow-ons, 100 million boe EUR. Builds on Thunder Horse South.

Appalachia Marcellus: 25,000 acres Susquehanna, 16 wells at 25 MMcf/d IP30s over 12,000-ft laterals, sub-$1.50/MMBtu breakevens. Piloting ResFrac FiberFlow for 15% SRV uplift.

Future plans: 45-50 Permian wells Q3, ramp to 65 Q1 2025 with third Delaware rig. Eagle Ford 12-15 quarterly, prioritizing Pearsall via ML seismic with TGS. GoM $150 million next year, $75 million Walker Ridge farm-down option.

Emphasizing efficiency: drilling $/ft down 11% to $950, completions $6.50/boe via ProFrac electric fleets (40% emissions cut). Inventory 4,200 locations, 15+ years. Hedged 60% 2025 oil at $75.50. Q2 growth 18% to 185,000 boe/d, Q3 exit 195,000.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Brian Walsh with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Brian Walsh: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the drivers behind your production beat this quarter?

David Thompson: Good morning, Brian. Absolutely. The outperformance was broad-based but led by Permian pads like Waha North, where Genesis designs delivered IP30s well above curve, combined with faster cycle times from our cube strategy. Eagle Ford liquids also surprised positively on refined fracs. We're on track for full-year growth, with Q3 ramping further on 14 rigs.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks. Good morning, team. I wanted to dive deeper into your future development plans and resource potential. With the recent reserve update, can you walk us through the inventory runway, key projects, and how you're positioning for the next cycle?

Alex Rivera: Absolutely, Sarah. Great question, and it's one we're getting a lot as investors look beyond near-term volatility. Let me take you through our forward development plans and resource potential. I'll start with the big picture on inventory, then regionally, technical initiatives, and capital allocation.

On resource potential: Year-end 2023 reserves audited by Ryder Scott show proved developed producing at 1.2 billion BOE, total proved 2.1 billion. 2P reserves at 4.8 billion BOE, up 15% YoY from delineations. Unrisked contingent 8.2 billion, total inventory over 13 billion BOE—25+ year runway at 500,000 BOE/d pace. NAV-10 at $65 WTI: $45/share, 2.1x current trading; $10 WTI adds $12/share.

2024 capex $4.2-4.5 billion: 60% development drilling, 25% facilities/infra, 10% exploration, 5% low-carbon. Guide 8-10% growth to 520-540 mBOE/d, 65% oil. 2025-2027 CAGR 12%, to 650-700 mBOE/d by 2028, FCF-funded at $60+ oil.

Regionally, Permian 55% production/65% inventory: 4,500 DRLs, 12,000-ft laterals, Wolfcamp A EUR 1.4 million bbls, Second Bone Spring 1.1 million—up 20% via cube dev (16-well pads). Drill times 8 days/well, F&D $7-8/BOE. Pecos River expansion: $800 million, 200 wells by Q4 '25, +40 mBOE/d, >60% IRRs.

Gulf of Mexico 20%: Winterfell discovery certified 500 million BOE 2P subsalt. Subsea tie-backs to Holstein, $1.2 billion, first oil mid-2026, peak 50 mBOE/d, <$40 breakeven. Lobster Q3 '24 well, 300 million upside. Recycle 3.5x industry.

Namibia Block Z-9 with TotalEnergies: Venus-1X 2 billion barrel column, 30% WI nets 400 million risked. FPSO 2026, first oil 2028, $25-30 breakeven, $3 billion NPV10.

North Sea UK: Clair Ridge Phase 2 +20 mBOE/d to 2030 via polymer EOR.

Technical: Digital rock/ML seismic with Schlumberger Delfi, success 92%. Dissolvable plugs/engineered proppants cut water 15%, IP30 +25%. Permian CO2 EOR pilots +10-15% recovery. Pecos CCUS 2 million tons/year by 2027 for 45Q.

Strategy: 80% capex Tier 1 >50% IRR. Opportunistic M&A post-Pioneer/Exxon. Hedging 60% 2024 oil $70 floor. Breakevens $42 corporate. 15% FCF yield, 50% returns. TIR >200% five years.

Our plans deliver growth, returns, optionality at $70-80 oil. Happy for follow-ups.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Good morning. Could you please provide more color on your Eagle Ford performance and plans there?

Maria Lopez: Good morning, Lisa. Eagle Ford remains a standout, with Q2 IP30s at 1,800 boe/d and 85% liquids, thanks to slickwater optimizations and ceramics reducing water cuts. We've de-risked more inventory there, holding steady at 12-15 wells per quarter, focusing on Pearsall hybrids. Takeaway is solid post-Enterprise expansions, supporting our sub-$40 breakevens.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to David Thompson for closing remarks.

David Thompson: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q2. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
